    Package index

    Run SigDoTS

    sigdots() runs the whole analysis and returns the result; sigdots_control() holds the settings that rarely need changing. Each page below explains the function, every argument with its allowed values and default, and what is returned.

    sigdots()
    Significance test for spatial domains
    sigdots_control()
    Settings of sigdots() that rarely need changing

    Prepare the input

    sigdots() takes a normalised expression matrix with coordinates, a Seurat object or a SpatialExperiment object directly. From raw counts, sigdots_prepare() makes the matrix.

    sigdots_prepare()
    Expression matrix for sigdots() from a counts matrix

    Read the result

    What print() and summary() show and how to read the split tree and the tests table; the domain of every spot as a table or written back into your object; the plots.

    print(<sigdots>) summary(<sigdots>) print(<summary.sigdots>)
    Print and summarise a SigDoTS result
    domains()
    The domain of every spot
    add_domains()
    Add the domains to a Seurat or SpatialExperiment object
    plot(<sigdots>)
    Plot a SigDoTS result
